key_big: Square both sides, then check every answer.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • g(x) = a√(b(x − c)) + d starts at the point (c, d).
  • x − c moves the graph right c; + d moves it up d.
  • a stretches or shrinks it vertically; a negative a reflects it over the x-axis. bx divides every x-coordinate by b; a negative b reflects it over the y-axis.
  • To solve a square root equation, get the root alone, square both sides, and check every answer: squaring can add extraneous solutions.

Examples

Example

√(x + 3) = x − 3

x + 3 = x2 − 6x + 9

x = 1 or x = 6

Check: x = 1 gives 2 = −2 ✗

Answer: x = 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Shifting the wrong way√(x − 4) moves right 4.
Multiplying by b√(2x) divides the x-coordinates by 2.
Not checkingAn answer that makes the root negative is extraneous.

Identify extraneous solutions of square root equations.
Squaring both sides can turn a false equation like 2 = −2 into a true one, 4 = 4.

items.q: The point (9, 3) is on the graph of f(x) = √x. Which point is on the graph of g(x) = √(−x)?
items.e: g(−9) = f(−1 · −9) = f(9) = 3. Divide the x-coordinate by −1 and keep the y-coordinate. (−9, 3).
